findings.quote: '80% range of 329 to 838': NOT shown. The dot column spans visibly wider than that ... the 80% range is not marked inside them
On first look I read them as labelling the dots (upper dots = expected, lower = received), not the two lines
Y ticks at 1K intervals for a series that lives between 600 and 1,400 for most of its length; nothing between 0 and 1K to read against
What is DSQ, and why this code? ... 'DSQ' by itself means nothing to the executive team
The band from Jan 2024 is described in the subtitle as an 80% range but has no on-plot legend entry
The title is about average error. The plot shows the raw series, not errors ... a reader who trusts the picture over the words will come away with 'both models look about the same'
The grey dotted line on the pale band is the faintest element and is the one the title compares against
The dashed lines run through the value labels: '71% of 24 months' has the 80% line through 'of'
Row labels carry a second variable ('trailing mean' / 'candidate') with no explanation on the plot ... on a phone you'd not know DSQ is on a different model to NIK
NIK at 100% of 24 months - that's a band that never misses, which usually means the band is too wide, and there's no width shown

PYX has adjacent squares at Jan-Feb 2024 and OZD has four consecutive squares Jan-Apr 2024. By the subtitle's own definition those look like episodes with no box ... by my count from the paragraph it is 22 of 30, which rather changes the title
counting diamonds off the plot I get about 21 ... Same-month recalls appear to overprint as one diamond, so 24 cannot be reached from the plot
There is no on-plot key for square / diamond / shaded box; it lives in the subtitle
The episode annotation sits at the top of the plot, two lanes above the DSP box, with no leader
the vertical dashed line is explained as a reporting change 'which does not apply to these codes', which raises the question of why it is on the chart at all
The x-axis collapsed to just 'Jan '22' and 'Sep '26', so I could no longer find the 2024 spike by date ... Axis labels collide: 'Jan '24Nov '24' runs together as one string
The 'rule off' tags disappeared from the lane labels, so on the phone there is no indication which lanes are disabled
The lanes compressed so hard that squares and diamonds overlap; on OZD and DSQ I could not separate them

the May 2026 dot sits inside the shaded 'incomplete' zone, and the annotation says shaded months are incomplete. The title then uses one of those months as a comparable figure ... The plot does not say that
'within 6' (grey dashed) and 'within 12' (grey solid) are hard to separate anywhere except the spikes ... Green solid and grey solid become two solid greys of similar weight
The green plunge to ~170 at Jul-Aug 2026 is the most visually dramatic thing on the chart and is an artefact; the annotation addresses it but sits at the top-right, away from the plunge
The annotation moves below the plot and is set in green while the dots it describes are blue, so the colour link is lost
The 'largest miss' annotation moved below the chart, so the peak had no label next to it, and the little orange vertical line was still there but now unexplained until I scrolled
I looked for what 'eligible' means and for how many reports were thrown out by the 'one firm-list exclusion' the source line mentions
The subtitle says 92% covered, so two months missed - May 2024 is one, and I couldn't tell which the other was
I also couldn't tell whether the band is the thing that generates a review flag or just a descriptive ribbon
Who decided 70% was the cut-off, when was that decided, and was it before or after these results came in?
I looked for the number of months, not just the percentage ... '33% of 24 months' I can turn into 8 myself, but I should not have to
For NPT, OZD and PYX, what are we doing instead? 'Rule off' means nobody is looking at those codes through this system
every mark is 'actual exceeded the range', so there's no mark for coming in under. Is that by design? ... where did 'five' come from?
Twenty-four Class I recalls in this span across these codes is a large number and the chart gives me no denominator for it
I couldn't tell from the picture whether the recall dates tended to come before or after the flagged months. I also looked for how many Class I recalls fell in a flagged month and didn't find it
A quarter of the reports have no event date and are 'counted beside the chart, not in it.' Are they in the forecast in chart 1?
I also couldn't find why the 'within 12 months' grey line has spikes (Jan 2022, Jan 2024) that the 3-month line doesn't
that spike around mid-2024 to over 2K sits well outside the shaded band - is that the kind of thing this is supposed to catch, or the kind of thing it misses?
I also wanted to see the actual September number to compare against ... then I want to know when it will

'Selection was frozen at 2023-12 and this test ran once' - that is the sentence I care about, and I want to see what evidences it. Is there a commit, a signed file, a date-stamped config? A chart saying 'ran once' is a claim, not a proof
I looked for the trailing mean's coverage or its band. There's a grey dotted line for it but no range, so the 92% is only comparable to itself
a rule that fires once in two and a half years across seven codes isn't a review queue, it's a smoke alarm with the battery out
There is also no explanation of the big spike in early 2022 near 2.8K; a reviewer will ask what that was and nothing on the chart answers it
The legend became 'exp.' and 'rec.', which I had to think about for a second ... 'mean' on its own is ambiguous
